reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that correlated random walks (CRW) in NFL weekly P&L signs deviate from i.i.d. assumptions, necessitating a modified ruin probability calculation. This leads to a streak-aware gate where the probability p of positive outcomes per season is estimated, and if |p - 0.5| > 0.05, indicating significant streak persistence, and if CRW ruin probability differs significantly from i.i.d., the system adopts the adaptive gate. The mathematical foundation lies in the equivalence of ruin probability under different stochastic processes. For play generation, the model uses formation-conditioned diffusion to simulate plausible plays, validated via Jensen-Shannon divergence. Finally, data pipelines must demonstrate measurable speedup and improved deduplication to justify adoption, ensuring computational efficiency without sacrificing data integrity.
